summary:
Building the dashboard section now.

I've been deep in Keikochō, a Japanese-learning app I built for myself, and most of the recent work has been about catching cases where the app looked correct but wasn't. The clearest one: the drill only ever checked whether I could *read* a word's kana before quizzing me on it, never whether I'd actually been *taught what it meant*. So it started asking "what time is it — seven o'clock" using a word I'd never seen. Fixing it meant adding a whole extra stage to the practice loop that just teaches new vocabulary and grades nothing, because scoring something you were never shown measures the app's pacing, not you.

A similar bug showed up in the UI. A misdirected tap kept opening the wrong lesson, and I burned time checking the routing logic, the API, even a desktop browser click — all fine. It turned out to be a design flaw: two buttons that are guaranteed to sit next to each other by construction (the lesson you just finished, and the one that opens next) were 35px tall with a 7px gap on a phone screen, well under Apple's 44px minimum tap target. The fix wasn't padding — I just removed one of the two buttons, since a bigger card elsewhere already went to the same place.

I've also been generating the illustration deck for the app — switched recently from running Stable Diffusion locally on an old Tesla P100 to Replicate's hosted API, mostly for speed (minutes instead of hours for a batch). It's not just "generate and ship," though: for word cards where a number IS the meaning, I learned the image model reliably miscounts anything past 5 or 6 — ask for 7 balls and it draws 6, or rounds to a neat grid of 9. Rephrasing the prompt as a shape ("one straight row of seven") instead of a bare number fixed it. For a card like お昼 vs お昼過ぎ (roughly "noon" vs "just past noon"), I ended up compositing a small day/night bar onto existing clock images with code rather than generating it — some things are cheaper and more reliable to draw with a script than to prompt for.

Elsewhere I've kept building out the internal MCP servers connecting my personal automation agent to things like email and financial tracking, and did a quick front-end build to give myself proper manual controls (seed locking, samplers, batch generation) over image generation instead of using a chat interface for it.
